items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I worked with The Association and The Fifth Dimension and Diana Ross, and I got to work with strings.

ctx.x: Thanks for saying that, because that was something I meant to ask about, is that not all arrangers must be great or capable conductors. How did you learn to conduct? Was it something you did in school also?

Well things that are in tempo, dance band or jazz band charts, the conducting is kind of a grand word for it, because what you do is get them started and get them stopped. And you kind of give a little bit of shading if they need some help, but supposedly all the dynamics are marked on the page and good studio players are very good at picking up stuff like that. So unless you’ve got something that’s out of tempo or with strings or something, there’s not much to it. I did learn to conduct strings in the late 60s.…
If you were writing a chart, or a string chart for The Fifth Dimension, did you get a recording of the tune that was like the rhythm track or something?
